items.stem: Match LIST-I with LIST-II. LIST-I (statisticians): A. P. C. Mahalanobis; B. R. C. Bose; C. S. N. Roy; D. D. G. Horvitz and D. J. Thompson. LIST-II (contributions): I. D² distance in multivariate analysis; II. Unbiased estimator for unequal-probability sampling without replacement; III. Union–intersection principle in multivariate testing; IV. Partially balanced incomplete block designs. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Recall each statistician's best-known contribution: P. C. Mahalanobis → D² distance in multivariate analysis; R. C. Bose → Partially balanced incomplete block designs; S. N. Roy → Union–intersection principle in multivariate testing; D. G. Horvitz and D. J. Thompson → Unbiased estimator for unequal-probability sampling without replacement. So the matching is A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II. Trap: each item of LIST-II is used exactly once, so fix the pairs you are sure of first.

items.stem: Arrange the following in order of their year of establishment, from oldest to latest: A. Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) B. Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) C. National Statistical Office (NSO) D. National Sample Survey (NSS) E. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Founding years: Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) 1931; National Sample Survey (NSS) 1950; Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) 1951; Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) 1999; National Statistical Office (NSO) 2019. Sorting them gives A, D, B, E, C. Trap: the NSO (2019) is the newest — it was formed by merging the CSO and the NSSO.
